image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a rocky substrate in an intertidal zone. The chiton has a distinct oval shape with a dorsal surface covered in eight overlapping calcareous plates that are greenish-grey with mottled patterns. These plates are surrounded by a brownish, hairy or spiny girdle (mantle). The surrounding environment includes wet rocks, barnacles, and small patches of algae.
